title: Easing
summary: Easing is the shape of change over time. The curve decides whether an interface feels immediate, mechanical, or alive.

title: Spring
summary: A spring describes motion with forces instead of a clock: stiffness pulls, damping resists, mass adds inertia. The duration is an outcome, not an input.

title: Scroll snap
summary: Scroll snap turns free scrolling into a set of resting positions. The gesture stays native; the layout decides where it is allowed to stop.

title: Scroll-linked animation
summary: A scroll-linked animation uses the scroll position as its clock. The motion is not timed; it is a direct readout of where the scroller is.

title: Popover
summary: A popover is a small surface the platform owns: it lives in the top layer, closes on Escape or a click outside, and hands focus back — none of which you have to write.

title: Command palette
summary: A command palette is a modal dialog wearing a search box. The filter is the easy part; the dialog semantics, the keyboard contract and the action registry are the product.

title: Hover
summary: Hover is a continuously-evaluated state of a pointing device, not an event: it matches the element under the pointer and every ancestor above it, which is why the gate, the gap, the close delay and the hit test matter more than the transition.

title: Focus state
summary: Focus is the single element that will receive the next keypress. The browser decides the order, the stops, the scroll and the ring — and all four are measurable, so guessing about them is optional.

title: Progressive disclosure
summary: Progressive disclosure reveals detail on demand. The real cost is not the extra click — 'hidden' has five meanings, and only some of them take the content out of the keyboard's way.

title: Shared-element transition
summary: A shared element transition carries one object between two states so the eye follows it. The web can do this now, but in a list the naming strategy decides whether the element travels or the whole transition silently fails.

title: Breadcrumbs
summary: A breadcrumb trail is a picture of where the current page sits in the site's hierarchy — a second navigation, not a record of how you got here. Most of its failure modes are invisible until you inspect the accessibility tree.

title: Container query
summary: A container query lets a component restyle itself from the size of its own parent, not the browser window. It is the difference between a page that is responsive and a component that is responsive.

title: Visual hierarchy
summary: Visual hierarchy is the deliberate ordering of what a viewer notices first, second, third. It is built from a small set of measurable differences — contrast, scale, and spacing — not from taste alone.

title: Skeleton

title: Shimmer
summary: Shimmer is the moving highlight swept across a skeleton. It reports that a request is alive, nothing more — and how you draw it decides whether the browser composites or repaints.
